Inner_Sanctum_movie: Inner Sanctum is a 1948 American horror mystery film directed by Lew Landers and starring Charles Russell and Mary Beth Hughes. based on the Simon & Schuster book series of the same name and the Inner Sanctum Mystery radio series. Morros, Samuel Rheiner and Walter Shenson.

Charles Russell acquits himself very well as the handsome stranger with a murderous secret hiding out at the local boarding house. Mary Beth Hughes plays one icy ice-blonde, but just how far will she go to protect him? Roscoe Ates is reasonably effective as the boy who knew too much, but his cloying, annoying acting (sadly typical of child actors in this period) is the film's main drawback. rv: A fascinating Universal Newsreel clip documenting mestizos from Oaxaca and indigenous people greeting president Avelardo Rodriguez and his wife. The narrator mispronouces the word "Oaxaca," which should really sound more like "Gua-ha-ka." The indigenous people are performing ancient Zapotec rituals, which include dancing for the celebration of the guelaguetza that takes place in the state of Oaxaca. The length of the clip does not undermine it's historical importance, in fact, its very existence makes it a constructive piece for further analysis on many fronts: cultural, social, ethnographic,

rv: The main advantage of this cartoon is it lets you know about old Popeye cartoons that aren't on archive.org yet

I love these old, 1930's era Popeye cartoons, as I've mentioned in several other Popeye reviews. In contrast, if you've watched the 1950's version of them, you immediately see that the 1950's version is far less funny, at least from a verbal point of view. Olive Oyl somehow retained her unbelievably great physical humor, but Popeye and Bluto lost theirs (Bluto also lost that terrific basso profundo voice of his). In addition, a whole host of side characters disappeared (if you have ever seen the Robin Wiiliams movie of Popeye you'll know what I mean). Those are some of the reasons I prefer the

This is the first Popeye I've seen where Wimpy plays a significant role in the story. I'm willing to forgive a plot that serves as a framing device to showcase other episodes to get an insight into this character's... uhm, character. :)
